name: Account deletion requirements
plain: Both stores require an in-app way to delete an account and its data if the app lets you create one.
meaning: Apple required in-app deletion from 30 June 2022 (plus Sign in with Apple token revocation). Google required a deletion path in the app and a web link from 8 December 2023, with Data safety disclosure, and enforcement from 2024.

android.store_policy: Play account deletion policy: in-app path plus web URL in Data safety; enforcement 2024
android.api_surface: Play Console > Data safety > Data deletion
android.note: Developer can retain data only as legally required and must disclose.

ios.store_policy: 5.1.1(v): in-app account deletion, not just deactivate; revoke Sign in with Apple tokens
ios.api_surface: App Store Connect account deletion; Sign in with Apple REST revoke

limits.headline: Can't keep your account forever, since apps must let you delete it in the app
limits.user_action: You open the app account settings and tap Delete account
can: Start the deletion of your account and data inside the app
Keep some data when a law requires it, with a note telling you
Point you to a web page for deletion (Android)
cannot: Hide the deletion option, if the app lets you create an account
Keep the data for no reason after you delete
Skip Sign in with Apple cleanup on iPhone
limits.differs: Apple required in app deletion from 30 June 2022. Google added a web link too, from 8 December 2023.

story.what_it_is: The rule that an app must let you delete your account and data, inside the app.

marketing.name: Offering account deletion in your app
marketing.pitch: If your app lets people create an account, it must also let them delete it.

marketing.name: Account deletion requirements
marketing.pitch: Apps must offer in app deletion and a web link where people can request it.

story.for_you: You find 'Delete account' in the app settings and it removes your profile and data. No email chain or phone call is needed.
story.for_makers: Both stores require the delete option, so makers must build the whole chain: delete data, revoke Sign in with Apple, and tell partners. It forces cleaner data design and cuts regulator risk.

use_cases.example: A social app puts 'Delete my account' under Settings and erases your posts after a short grace period.
A dating app lets you delete the account and cancel the subscription steps are explained.
A game warns that deleting the account also wipes all purchases and progress.
A store app removes saved cards and order history when you delete.
A fintech app deletes your profile but keeps required transaction records by law and says so.
A team revokes the Sign in with Apple token when you delete, as Apple requires.

story.android_note: Google Play also requires a web link, so you can delete without having the app installed.
story.ios_note: Apple required it from 30 June 2022 and added Sign in with Apple token revocation.

abuse: Dark patterns that hide the option

history.change: Account deletion path and web link required from 8 December 2023
